fullText:
Disney invoked 9 U.S.C. § 3 to seek a halt to a wrongful-death lawsuit—with a streaming signup in its argument.

Disney linked Jeffrey Piccolo’s Disney+ free-trial acceptance to later park-ticket terms, seeking individual arbitration and a stay of court proceedings. Piccolo argued that conflicting parks terms favored court and that his personal acceptance did not bind his wife’s estate. Disney subsequently abandoned arbitration, and Piccolo later voluntarily dismissed the lawsuit; neither development establishes that Disney’s contractual theory was enforceable.

Receipt: Orange County, Florida, case 2024-CA-001616-O; Disney’s May 31, 2024 motion to compel arbitration, Background § 2, quoting the Subscriber Agreement: “any dispute between You and Us, Except for Small Claims, is subject to a class action waiver and must be resolved by individual binding arbitration.” The motion also invokes Disney Terms of Use § 7.

Before accepting, save the linked terms. Check which affiliates and services they cover, whose consent they claim, and which document controls conflicts. Arbitration concerns the forum—not immunity: the filed terms expressly allow individual damages. Do not treat the lawsuit’s dismissal as proof of a payout.
